subject: pharmacology
title: Chelators and Antidotes: Dimercaprol, EDTA, Iron Chelators, Penicillamine and Poisoning Antidotes

steps.tx: **Dimercaprol** (BAL, British anti Lewisite) offers two sulfhydryl groups that out compete tissue enzymes for arsenic, mercury and lead, forming renally excreted chelates, given by painful deep intramuscular injections in peanut oil with hypertension, tachycardia, fever and vomiting ledgers, and forbidden in iron and cadmium poisoning where its chelates are more toxic than the metal. It opens chelation's governing rule: the complex must be safer than the poison.
steps.say: BAL rescues arsenic and lead by sulfhydryl competition; with iron its chelate is worse than the metal.

vis.alt: Heavy metal poisoning clinical manifestations diagram for lead arsenic and mercury
vis.caption: Heavy metal poisoning manifestations, the poisonings chelators are matched against.

steps.tx: **Succimer** (DMSA) is BAL's oral water soluble heir for lead poisoning (children with levels above thresholds, encephalopathy adding parenteral partners), gentler in every ledger, while **calcium disodium EDTA** chelates lead extracellularly in severe poisoning combined with BAL in encephalopathy, billing nephrotoxicity and the fatal error of using disodium EDTA whose calcium stripping stops hearts. The EDTA salt distinction is a prescription safety examination in itself.
steps.say: Calcium disodium EDTA saves lead poisoned brains; the wrong EDTA salt stops hearts.

left.title: Lead ladder
points: Succimer oral for moderate paediatric elevations
Remove source: chelation without abatement fails

right.title: EDTA safety
points: Calcium disodium salt only for chelation

steps.tx: **Lead poisoning** itself is the clinical frame: colic, anaemia with basophilic stippling, wrist drop, encephalopathy in children whose developing brains absorb more and forgive less, managed by source removal first (paint, water, occupation, traditional remedies), chelation by level and symptoms, and public health notification because one child indexes an environment poisoning others. Drugs finish what abatement starts.
steps.say: Chelate the child, then remove the paint; treating without abatement is a revolving door.

steps.tx: **Desferrioxamine**, a bacterial siderophore given parenterally, founded iron chelation for transfusion overloaded thalassaemia (nightly subcutaneous infusions), billing infusion hypotension, Yersinia sepsis susceptibility (the chelator feeds the bacterium iron), hearing, eye and growth ledgers, succeeded by oral **deferasirox** (daily, renal and hepatic monitoring, gastrointestinal bleeding) and **deferiprone** (agranulocytosis surveillance, arthropathy), chosen and combined by cardiac iron (T2 star MRI) arithmetic.
steps.say: Three chelators, one overloaded heart; MRI iron, not ferritin alone, writes the prescription.

right.title: Oral successors
points: Deferasirox: renal, liver, GI bleed monitoring
Chelation holidays when iron burden falls

steps.tx: **Penicillamine** chelates copper in Wilson disease (from the copper lesson: decoppering until maintenance, zinc as the gentler rival), bills autoimmune syndromes (pemphigus, lupus like, myasthenia), proteinuria and marrow suppression demanding surveillance, and worsens neurology transiently when started as copper mobilises. Its cystinuria second career (solubilising cystine stones) completes an unusually examinable profile.
steps.say: Penicillamine decoppers Wilson patients and bills autoimmunity; zinc inherited its gentler half.

left.title: Wilson deployment
points: Decoppering phase then maintenance or zinc swap
Trientine the better tolerated chelator alternative

right.title: Penicillamine ledger
points: Taste loss and skin wrinkling minor

steps.tx: **Atropine** and **pralidoxime** answer organophosphates from the cholinergic lessons: atropine titrated to drying secretions (not pupil size) in escalating doubling doses, pralidoxime reactivating phosphorylated acetylcholinesterase before ageing (hours, compound dependent) as an atropine adjunct, benzodiazepines for seizures, and decontamination protecting staff. Naloxone (opioid) and flumazenil (benzodiazepine, seizure fenced) complete the receptor antidote triad examinations recite.
steps.say: Atropine to dry lungs, oxime before ageing, naloxone for opioids; pupils never guide atropine.

left.title: Organophosphate pair
points: Atropine doubling doses to clear chest
Intermediate syndrome and delayed neuropathy watched

right.title: Receptor antidotes
points: Naloxone: titrated to breathing, renarcotisation watched
Flumazenil: avoided in dependence and mixed overdose
Atropine also answers muscarinic mushroom and drug excess

steps.tx: **N-acetylcysteine**, **fomepizole** and **hydroxocobalamin** anchor the metabolic antidotes: NAC replenishes glutathione for paracetamol (nomogram timed from the analgesic lessons), fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase in methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning (ethanol the older rival), and hydroxocobalamin binds cyanide in smoke inhalation turning blood and urine port wine red. Each antidote's clock is its pharmacology: NAC by hours, fomepizole before acids accumulate, hydroxocobalamin at the fire scene.
steps.say: Metabolic antidotes race clocks: glutathione by hours, acid prevention by enzyme blockade, cyanide at the scene.

left.title: NAC and fomepizole
points: NAC: paracetamol nomogram, IV or oral protocols
Dialysis thresholds by acidosis and organ injury

right.title: Cyanide antidotes
points: Red discoloration interferes with colorimetric labs

steps.tx: **Methylene blue** reduces methaemoglobin (from the haemolysis lessons) at 1 to 2 mg per kg intravenously, forbidden fruitlessly in G6PD deficiency where its oxidant stress haemolyses and incapable without NADPH, while serving vasoplegic shock and ifosfamide encephalopathy niches, and turning urine blue green as its calling card. Antidote literacy is matching mechanism to poison under time pressure, which this whole lesson rehearses.
steps.say: Methylene blue needs NADPH to work; in G6PD deficiency it becomes the oxidant problem itself.

nodes.label: Antidote matched: chelator, antagonist or metabolic
Clock checked: NAC hours, oxime ageing, chelation thresholds
Supportive care and poison centre partnership throughout
